column1: # The frozen contract requires "all twelve ordered pairs of the four
# generations on the frozen fixture, plus the anti-self-reference and
# Each pair is compared with `diff` over the per-row records of the
# two generations.  A disagreement is counted from the diff's '<' lines.
# The comparison is ORDERED: G0->G1 and G1->G0 are separate rows.
# THE COUNTS ARE DERIVED, NOT ASSERTED
# The row count in every pair is 21, which is the fixture's own row
# count.  No pair compared a truncated row set.
# row_id_order_identical  the two runs present the rows in the SAME
#                         ORDER and with the SAME row ids.
# input_pair_identical    the (token_type, keyword_id) pair of every
#                         row is the same in both runs.
# expected_identical      the expected selector of every row is the
#                         same in both runs -- it comes from the
# observed_identical      the OBSERVED selector of every row is the
#                         same in both runs -- this is the actual
# A pair that agreed only on the expected column would be vacuous;
# the observed column is the one that carries the authority claim.
# The four runs are NOT four copies of one run:
#   * G0 executes the REAL legacy C chain (src/parser.c with the
#     candidate selector OFF), a DIFFERENT language, a DIFFERENT
#     producer and a DIFFERENT object from the three PolyC runs.
#   * G1, G2 and G3 each execute a SEPARATE COMPILATION of the PolyC
#     component by a DIFFERENT producer binary.
#   * The comparison layer is the same object, so the equality is not
#     an artefact of the comparison code.
# The RECON08 producer-identity control (R8-PV-01) requires a
# relabelled producer to be rejected; the SLICE09-owned equivalent is
